subject: CareSync pilot: MAP milestones, acceptance checkpoints & closure path
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@caresync.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: CareSync pilot: MAP milestones, acceptance checkpoints & closure path

Hi Samira,

Thanks again for the productive demo yesterday. As discussed, I’ve attached an initial mutual action plan (MAP) and a short outline of acceptance tests so we have a single point of truth for the pilot run and signoff. The goal here is to make the evaluation deterministic so your team can sign off quickly if we meet the criteria.

High-level milestones (proposed):
- Week 1 (Feb 23–28): Provisioning & connectivity, dataset handoff, baseline smoke tests
- Week 2 (Mar 1–7): Integration + latency/throughput runs on representative traffic
- Week 3 (Mar 8–14): Production-sim smoke tests, user-facing concordance checks
- Week 4 (Mar 15–21): Acceptance run & signoff; procurement issues PO for Dedicated if green

Acceptance checkpoints (examples):
- Latency: p95 generation <= 350ms on 1k-token median request (see test details)
- Quality: F1-style concordance on labeled prompt set >= 92% (sample size = 500)
- Errors: <= 0.3% inference errors/exceptions during a 2-hour steady-state run

Please review the attached MAP ("mutual_action_plan_v1.xlsx") and the test outline ("evaluation_test_cases.md"). A few asks:
1) Confirm the sample prompt set for the concordance test (we expect ~500 items; can use the sample you shared or we can expand it).
2) Confirm the procurement timeline (you mentioned early March for PO?)
3) Any additional success signals you want included (security, data retention checks, etc.)

I’ll loop in Lauren for the acceptance test runbook and Marcus for the smoke schedule.

Link to the live doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-CareSync-MAP

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mutual_action_plan_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: evaluation_test_cases.md (text)]
From: Samira Khan <samira@caresync.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Blake <tom@caresync.com>, procurement@caresync.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CareSync pilot: MAP milestones, acceptance checkpoints & closure path

On Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 9:12 AM Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Samira,
> 
> Thanks again for the productive demo yesterday...

Hi Jordan — thanks for pulling this together. High level looks good. A few clarifying questions before we finalize the MAP: 

- For the concordance F1 target, can you confirm whether that metric includes hallucination penalization? We want the evaluators to treat any unsupported assertion as a fail.
- On latency: are the latency numbers measured from a regional VPC ingress? Our traffic will originate in us-west-2.
- Security/compliance: procurement needs a short list of SOC2/ISO artifacts you can share with us (at minimum: SOC2 Type II, data retention policy, and encryption-at-rest details).

Procurement note: procurement@caresync.com is on copy. We aim to have an internal approval by Feb 28, with PO by Mar 5 if acceptance criteria are met.

Last: is there a lightweight test harness we can run on our environment to sanity-check integrations before you provision dedicated capacity?

Thanks — I’ll review the doc and get back with a suggested prompt sample by EOD Friday.

— Samira
Head of Product | CareSync Health
[Signature block]
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@caresync.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CareSync pilot: MAP milestones, acceptance checkpoints & closure path

Hi Samira — quick answers to your questions (and adding concrete test ownership):

- Concordance metric: yes — any unsupported assertion is treated as a false positive and counted against the F1. We’ll provide the scoring script we’ll run (deterministic rubric). See "evaluation_runbook.pdf" attached.
- Latency baseline: tests will be run from us-west-2. Our internal test agents will generate the traffic from a customer VPC mirror in us-west-2 so the numbers reflect regional ingress. We’ll include both cold-start and steady-state p95 numbers.
- Compliance artifacts: we can share a redacted SOC2 Type II summary, encryption-at-rest architecture diagram, and our retention policy. I’ll send those to procurement directly.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Redwood: provide evaluation runbook, host the site under a dedicated evaluation environment, and run the controlled latency/throughput tests (Marcus).
- CareSync: provide labeled prompt set, approve the concordance rubric, and run the local integration sanity harness.

Test harness: yes — we’ll provide a 2-script harness (sanity + smoke) that runs locally against your staging endpoints; small Python bundle and a README. That will be posted to the shared doc.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) CareSync to upload final prompt sample by Feb 13 EOD.
2) Redwood to provision evaluation environment by Feb 23 and run a 1-hour smoke test on Feb 24.
3) Full acceptance run Mar 15.

Attaching runbook and compliance artifact pointers.

— Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: evaluation_runbook.pdf (pdf)]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@caresync.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>

On Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 2:20 PM Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Samira — quick answers to your questions...

Folks — I’m scheduling the smoke window and will own the initial run:
- Provisioning window: Feb 23–24 (we’ll hand you the staging endpoint and credentials).
- Smoke run: Feb 24 10:00–11:30 PST (1.5h) — we’ll run connectivity, simple throughput, and error-rate checks.
- Latency bench runs (steady-state): Mar 2–3 (we’ll provide raw logs and p95/p99 values).

I’ll upload a sample of the smoke-run CSV output to the doc after the Feb 24 run (example: "smoke-test-results-sample.csv"). Please ensure your staging team has:
- IP allowlist (we’ll provide IPs 24 hours before provisioning)
- Credential ingestion steps from the README in the shared doc

If anyone needs to shift the window, call it out by Feb 20.

— Marcus Lin
SRE Lead, Inference Operations | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: smoke-test-results-sample.csv (csv)]
From: Samira Khan <samira@caresync.com>

Thanks team — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A couple of confirmations from CareSync: 

- We’ll finalize and upload the 500-item prompt sample to the shared doc by Feb 20 EOD.
- Procurement confirms internal approval timeline of Feb 28 and will aim to issue PO by Mar 5 contingent on acceptance.
- Security would like the SOC2 summary and retention policy; procurement@caresync.com, please work with Lauren directly.

Once we have the staging endpoint on Feb 23 and the smoke run on Feb 24, we’ll do a short internal review and confirm if we proceed to the full acceptance run on Mar 15. If all goes well, this should set us up for a Dedicated capacity PO.

Appreciate the clarity — please add the final dates to the MAP and we’ll sign the document as the next step.

— Samira Khan
Head of Product | CareSync Health
